passages.title: Gear Grinders News
sentences: Welcome to the March newsletter of the Gear Grinders, the robotics club at Harbor Middle School.
This month, our biggest event is the Harbor Town Rover Race on Saturday, March 22, in the school gym.
Each team will drive a small rover through a course of ramps, tunnels and one narrow bridge.
The judges will time each run, but they will also give points for careful driving and clear teamwork.
To enter the race, each team must hand in an entry form to Ms. Ortiz by Friday, March 14.
A team needs three or four members, and every member needs a safety agreement signed by a parent.
Priya Shah's team has already finished its rover, which uses two motors and a light sensor.
Teams that are still building can use the club workshop on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 3:15 PM to 5:00 PM.
Please remember the workshop rules.
Wear safety glasses whenever anyone at your table is cutting, drilling or soldering.
Charge batteries on the metal tray by the window, and never inside a backpack.
Clean your table ten minutes before the workshop closes, so the room can be locked on time.
Finally, we need helpers to set up the race course on the morning of the race.
If you can help from 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM, write your name on the sign-up sheet outside Room 12.

passages.title: Welcome to the Model Railroad Club
sentences: Welcome to the Harbor Town Model Railroad Club, which meets in the basement of the Harbor Town Library.
Our layout is a model of the coast, with a working drawbridge, a ferry dock and a tunnel under Lantern Peaks.
Junior members are 11 to 15 years old, and each one works with an adult member called a crew partner.
Your crew partner will teach you how the layout works and will sign your logbook after each lesson.
Regular meetings are on Saturdays from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.
During June, however, meetings will move to Wednesdays from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM.
The library needs the basement for its summer reading camp on Saturday mornings in June.
Meetings return to Saturday mornings on the first Saturday in July.
Before you can run a train on your own, you need three signatures in your logbook.
You earn the first one for learning the track map, the second for using the control panel, and the third for a safe practice run.
Most junior members earn all three signatures in four to six meetings.
Members with three signatures may run a train at our Open House on Saturday, July 12, when families visit the layout.
Please follow these rules to keep the trains and the layout in good shape.
Wash your hands before you touch a train, because oil and dust from your fingers can clog the tiny motors.
Never reach across the track while a train is moving; walk around the table instead.
Food and drinks stay upstairs in the lobby, and backpacks go on the shelf by the door.
If you have a question, ask your crew partner or email the club at trains@example.com.
We are glad you joined, and we hope you enjoy your first season with us.

passages.title: Game Club News
sentences: Welcome to the October newsletter of the Harbor Middle School Game Club.
We meet every Friday from 3:15 PM to 4:45 PM in the school library.
Members can play board games, card games and video games on the club's two consoles.
Each console has a sign-up sheet on the wall, and each turn lasts 20 minutes.
Our big event this month is the Harbor Puzzle Cup on Friday, October 24.
Players will work in pairs to solve the puzzle levels in a game called Lighthouse Logic.
The pair that finishes the most levels in 30 minutes will have their names put on the club trophy.
To enter, write both names on the tournament sheet by Wednesday, October 22.
If you do not have a partner yet, write only your name, and Ben Diaz will help you find one.
Please remember the club rules.
Wipe your hands before you use a controller, because many people share them.
Put every game piece back in its box before you leave, and count the cards in each deck.
Use quiet voices, because other students are reading in the library.
Phones stay in backpacks during club time.
One more thing: the library is closed on Friday, October 17, for the book fair.
That day only, Game Club will meet in Room 8, and there will be no video games.
The consoles cannot be moved, but the board games and card games will be in Room 8.
See you on Friday!

visual.subject: Ridgeway Mine Museum trip: storm changes
rows: Dear Rock Club families,
A strong storm is expected this Saturday, November 8, so our trip to the Ridgeway Mine Museum must change.
Heavy rain can flood the lower tunnel of the mine, and the museum closes the tunnel tour when that happens.
The trip is now on Saturday, November 15, one week later.
We will still meet at the Harbor Town bus station at 8:30 AM, and we will still be back by 3:00 PM.
The cost is still $12. If you already paid, you do not need to pay again.
One activity has changed. The outdoor gem-panning stream closes for the winter on November 10.
Instead, members will take an indoor class about how crystals form, and each member will take home a piece of quartz.
Because it will be colder, we will eat our packed lunches in the museum's lunchroom instead of at the picnic tables.
The tunnel stays at about 50°F all year, so everyone needs a warm jacket.
The museum lends every visitor a hard hat. Please wear closed shoes with good grip, because the tunnel floor is wet.
If your child cannot come on November 15, please email me by Wednesday, November 12.
If I do not hear from you, I will count your child as coming.
Thank you for being flexible. Mr. Varga

items.explain: Sam needs three signatures in his logbook. The third paragraph says members with three signatures may run a train at the Open House, and the first paragraph says his crew partner signs the logbook. Four to six meetings is only how long it usually takes.

items.prompt: Sam wants to buy 3 small rocks at the show. How much money does he need?
items.hint: Find the message that gives the price of one small rock. Then count 3 of them.
items.explain: Sam needs $3. The fourth message says small rocks cost $1 each, and 3 rocks at $1 each is $3.

items.prompt: Who will drive Sam and Maya to the show?
options: Sam's dad
Maya's mom
Mr. Okafor
items.hint: The text is from Maya. Find the word my. When Maya writes my, she means herself.
items.explain: Maya's mom will drive them. Maya wrote the text, so My mom can drive us means Maya's mom. It is in the third message.

items.prompt: Ana has band practice on Thursday, May 8. Where should she go, and when does practice start?
options: The music room at 3:15 PM
The music room at 3:30 PM
The cafeteria stage at 3:15 PM
The cafeteria stage at 3:30 PM
items.hint: The plan changed. Check that May 8 is inside the two weeks. Then find the new place and the new start time.
items.explain: Ana should go to the cafeteria stage at 3:30 PM. The third line says practice is on the stage from May 6 to May 15, and the fourth line says it now starts at 3:30 PM instead of 3:15 PM.

items.prompt: Ana's dad asks when band goes back to the music room. Tap the line that tells him.
items.hint: Look for a line with the words music room and a date after the two weeks.
items.explain: Tap the line that says the band will be back in the music room on Tuesday, May 20. It is near the end of the email.

items.prompt: Maya plays the flute in the band. What should she do with her flute after practice?
options: Leave it on the stage
Take it home with her
Leave it in the music room
Give it to Ms. Gray
items.hint: The email puts instruments in two groups. Find the group that names flutes.
items.explain: Maya should take her flute home. The line about small instruments names flutes and says they go home with you after each practice. Only big instruments, like drums, stay on the stage.

items.prompt: Sam packs his bag for space camp. Sort each thing.
items.hint: The email has a pack list and a leave-at-home list. Chips are a kind of snack. Check each card against both lists.
items.explain: Pack the sleeping bag, the red flashlight and the warm sweater. They are on the pack list. Leave the tablet, the chips and the video game at home, because the email says to leave tablets, video games and snacks.

items.prompt: Today is Friday, June 27. The Rivera family has not sent the health form yet. What should they do?
options: Send it by Monday, June 30
Bring it to camp on Monday, July 7
Send it when camp ends on July 9
Pack it in Sam's bag
items.hint: The email has three dates. Find the line about the health form and read its date.
items.explain: They should send it by Monday, June 30. The line about the health form gives that date. July 7 is the day camp starts, which is too late.

items.prompt: Sam has $15 of birthday money. How much can he bring to camp?
options: All $15
Up to $10
Only $1
None, because camp gives campers everything
items.hint: Find the line about the camp shop. Look for the words up to.
items.explain: Sam can bring up to $10. The line about the camp shop says you may bring up to $10 for a patch or a poster. Camp gives meals, not shop items.

items.prompt: Today is Thursday, October 16. Ben's slip is signed, and his mom will pay with cash. What does Ben need to do, and by when?
options: Give the slip and $6 in an envelope to Mr. Lee by Friday, October 17
Give the slip to Mr. Lee by Wednesday, October 22, and pay on the bus
Give the slip and $6 to Ms. Ortiz by Friday, October 17
Give the slip to Mr. Lee by Friday, October 17, and pay at the museum
items.hint: Two parts of the slip matter here. Find who gets the slip and by when. Then find how to pay with cash.
items.explain: Ben gives the slip and $6 in an envelope to Mr. Lee by Friday, October 17. The Return to line names Mr. Lee and the date, and Part B says to put cash in an envelope with the slip. October 22 is the trip day.

items.prompt: Ben's mom wants to come on the trip as a helper. What should she write on the slip, and how much does she pay for her bus seat?
options: Her name in Part A, and $6 for her seat
Her name and phone number in Part D, and $6 for her seat
Her name and phone number in Part D, and nothing for her seat
Her signature in Part E, and nothing for her seat
items.hint: Find the part of the slip about adult helpers. Read all of it, including what it says about the bus.
items.explain: She writes her name and phone number in Part D and pays nothing for her seat. Part D asks helpers for a name and phone number and says helpers ride the bus for free. The $6 in Part B is Ben's cost.

items.prompt: Ben planned to bring juice in a glass bottle and buy a snack at the museum. What should he change?
options: Bring $5 to buy a snack at the museum
Keep the glass bottle, but wrap it in his jacket
Bring a drink with no glass, and pack all his food from home
Eat his snack on the bus on the way to the museum
items.hint: Find the part of the slip about lunch. It has two rules that touch Ben's plan. Fix both parts.
items.explain: Ben should bring a drink with no glass and pack all his food from home. Part C says no glass bottles or jars, and no food is sold at the museum.

items.prompt: Maya wants to play in the tournament, but she has no partner yet. What should she do?
options: Wait until she finds a partner, then sign up on October 24
Write only her name on the tournament sheet by October 22
Write her name on a console sign-up sheet on the wall
Ask Ben Diaz to play in the tournament for her
items.hint: Read the paragraph about the tournament. Find the sentence for players who have no partner, and the date to sign up.
items.explain: Maya should write only her name on the tournament sheet by October 22. The second paragraph says players with no partner write only their name, and Ben Diaz helps them find one.

items.prompt: Sam wants to play video games at Game Club on Friday, October 17. What will he find that day?
options: Club in the library, with video games as usual
No club at all, because of the book fair
Club in Room 8, with board games and card games but no video games
Club in Room 8, with the two consoles moved there
items.hint: Read the last paragraph. Find what is different on that day and what stays the same.
items.explain: Sam will find club in Room 8, with board games and card games but no video games. The last paragraph says the library is closed that day and the consoles cannot be moved.

items.prompt: Leo just finished a card game. Tap the sentence that tells him what to do before he leaves.
items.hint: Find the paragraph about club rules. Look for the word leave.
items.explain: Tap the sentence that says to put every game piece back in its box before you leave and count the cards in each deck. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Leo plays the drums in the Grade 7 band. What should he bring, and by what time should he arrive?
options: His drums and his music folder, by 6:00 PM
His drum sticks and his music folder, by 5:45 PM
His drum sticks and his music folder, by 6:00 PM
His drum sticks and a folding chair, by 6:30 PM
items.hint: Find the arrival time for Leo's grade. Then read the two lines about what band members bring, and check the rule for drummers.
items.explain: Leo should bring his drum sticks and his music folder and arrive by 6:00 PM. The Grade 7 band arrives at 6:00 PM, every band member brings a music folder, and drummers bring only their sticks because the drums are set up.

items.prompt: At 3:00 PM on May 29, the school texts: "It is raining. Use the rain plan." Where should Leo's family go to watch, and when does the concert start?
options: The bandstand in Harbor Park, at 6:30 PM
The school gym, at 6:30 PM
The school gym, at 7:45 PM
Nowhere, because the concert is canceled
items.hint: Find the line that starts with If it rains. Read what changes and what stays the same.
items.explain: They should go to the school gym, and the concert starts at 6:30 PM. The rain line says the concert moves to the gym and the start time stays the same. 7:45 PM is when it ends.

items.prompt: Maya's mom reads every line. Which plan is right for Maya now?
options: November 8, bus station at 8:30 AM, with a packed lunch and a warm jacket
November 15, bus station at 8:30 AM, with a packed lunch and a warm jacket
November 15, bus station at 8:30 AM, with a packed lunch and a pan for gem panning
November 15, museum gate at 8:30 AM, with a warm jacket and $12 for lunch
items.hint: Check four things one at a time: the new day, the meeting place, what is still happening, and what to bring.
items.explain: Maya goes on November 15 to the bus station at 8:30 AM, with a packed lunch and a warm jacket. The new date is in the fourth line, the bus station and time stay the same, the lunch line says packed lunches, and the tunnel line says to bring a warm jacket. Gem panning is closed, and November 8 is the old date.

items.prompt: Maya wants to know what is different now. Sort each part of the trip.

cards.text: Panning for gems in the stream
Meeting at the bus station at 8:30 AM

items.hint: Look for signal words. Still and same show what stayed. Now, instead and changed show what is different.
items.explain: The day, the gem panning and the lunch place changed. The trip is now on November 15, a crystal class replaces gem panning, and lunch is in the lunchroom instead of at the picnic tables. The bus station meeting, the $12 cost and the 3:00 PM return are still the same.

items.prompt: Maya's family will be away visiting her grandpa on November 15, so Maya cannot go. What should her family do?
options: Do nothing, because Mr. Varga will see that Maya is not at the bus station
Email Mr. Varga on the morning of November 15
Email Mr. Varga by Wednesday, November 12
Take Maya to the museum on November 8 instead
items.hint: Find the line for a child who cannot come on the new date. Then read the next line to see what happens if nobody writes.
items.explain: Maya's family should email Mr. Varga by Wednesday, November 12. The email asks for that, and the next line says that if he hears nothing, he will count Maya as coming.

items.prompt: On Saturday night, Ben reads the whole chat. Where is the game, and what time should he get there?
options: Pier Field, at 2:00 PM on Sunday
The school field, at 1:15 PM on Sunday
Pier Field, at 9:15 AM on Saturday
Pier Field, at 1:15 PM on Sunday
items.hint: Find the newest message about the game. Then find how early players arrive, and count back from the start time.
items.explain: Ben should get to Pier Field at 1:15 PM on Sunday. Change 2 moves the game to Sunday at 2:00 PM at Pier Field, and players arrive 45 minutes early. 2:00 PM minus 45 minutes is 1:15 PM.

items.prompt: Put Ben's soccer week in order, using the newest plans.
steps: Go to practice at the field behind the gym on Wednesday at 5:00 PM.
Eat Grandma's birthday lunch on Sunday.
Get to Pier Field at 1:15 PM to warm up.
Play the Gulls at 2:00 PM, wearing blue.
items.hint: Put the days in order first. Then, on Sunday, put the times in order.
items.explain: First Ben goes to practice at the school field on Wednesday, because of change 1. On Sunday he eats Grandma's lunch, gets to Pier Field at 1:15 PM, and plays at 2:00 PM, because of change 2.

items.prompt: Ana tells Grandma why the plans changed. Fill in each part.
items.frame: Practice moved because {0}. The game moved because {1}.

slots.label: Why practice moved
options: the town is cutting the grass at Pier Field
thunderstorms are in the forecast
the Gulls wear white

slots.label: Why the game moved
options: the town is cutting the grass at Pier Field
thunderstorms are in the forecast
players must warm up

items.hint: Find the two messages that start with Change. Each one gives a reason.
items.explain: Practice moved because the town is cutting the grass at Pier Field. The game moved because thunderstorms are in the forecast. Coach Novak gives each reason in Change 1 and Change 2.

steps.say: The question asks where. So I look for a place in the text.
I read each message. The second one says Meet me.
After the words Meet me at comes the place: the gym door.
The message also says 4:00 PM. That is a time, and the question asks where, so I use the place.
Sam should meet Mom at the gym door.
